nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What was the purpose of pooling data from two locations within the habitat?
nodes.answer: To increase detection to permissible levels and capture a broad range of species without over-parameterizing the models.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Community conservation|Community wildlife monitoring_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What physiological marker is commonly used to study avian stress in relation to human impact?
nodes.answer: Corticosterone is the physiological marker commonly used to study avian stress associated with human impact.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Community conservation|Community wildlife monitoring_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What challenges do species identification techniques face?
nodes.answer: Species identification techniques can perform sub-optimally when monitoring communities with multiple overlapping vocalizing species or in environments with numerous background noises.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Community conservation|Community wildlife monitoring_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the purpose of the BIOMON project?
nodes.answer: The purpose of the BIOMON project was to explore the effectiveness of acoustic indices in monitoring bird communities in biodiverse sites.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Community conservation|Community wildlife monitoring_qna_004
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: Which program is coordinated by BirdLife Cyprus for monitoring birds?
nodes.answer: The Common Birds Monitoring Scheme (CBMS) is coordinated by BirdLife Cyprus for monitoring birds.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Community conservation|Community wildlife monitoring_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the main objective of the paper discussed in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The main objective of the paper is to introduce the Multi-Modal Language Model technique to the bioacoustics community and to examine its potential and limitations.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Community conservation|Community wildlife monitoring_qna_006
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What new monitoring strategy is being developed as described in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The new strategy combines non-invasive field sampling using baited tubes to collect fecal pellets and molecular species determination utilizing the mitochondrial COI gene as a barcoding marker.
